Quality evaluation methods inherited from stereo and multichannel listening
tests assume a seated, passive listener. Interactive virtual environments break
that assumption: participants move, look around, and their exploration
behaviour is itself evidence about what they perceive.

**QoEVAVE** and its successor **EVOLVE-QoE** exist to close that gap — building
a methodological framework for evaluating quality of experience in interactive
audiovisual scenes, together with the tooling and open content other labs need
to apply it.

## My role

I joined as the PhD student on the project and now continue on it as a
postdoctoral researcher. My work runs from the evaluation methodology itself
through to the software and content that make it reproducible. I also
co-authored the EVOLVE-QoE funding application with the partner principal
investigator, and helped conceptualise the project's focus.

EVOLVE-QoE is a three-year collaborative project with a partner university,
funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG).

## Outputs

The project website is the canonical home for all of these:

- **QExE Tool** — a Quality of Experience evaluation toolkit
  ([project site](https://qoevave.github.io/qexe/))
- **QoEVAVE Database** — evaluation content for interactive virtual environments
  ([project site](https://qoevave.github.io/database/))
- **Cave, Cinema, and Mansion** — CGI scenes for interactive audio research
  ([AES](https://www.aes.org/e-lib/browse.cfm?elib=22518))
- **Audiovisual 360° database** — 360° video with higher-order ambisonics
  ([DOI](https://doi.org/10.1109/qomex55416.2022.9900893))
- **Influence of multi-modal interactive formats** on audio quality and
  exploration behaviour ([DOI](https://doi.org/10.1145/3573381.3596155))
